To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) insulin stimulates lipid synthesis in hepatocytes and this effect is not dependent on the presence of extracellular calcium; (2) vanadate also enhances lipid synthesis, but its effect is about 2-4 times higher than that induced by insulin; (3) ouabain significantly decreases lipid synthesis; (4) the stimulatory effects of insulin and vanadat are not mediated by changes in cytoplasmic calcium concentration.
Insulin and vanadate stimulate lipid synthesis in isolated rat liver cells.
Insulin and vanadate stimulate lipid synthesis, but not by increasing Ca2+ flux through the plasma membrane.

the effects of insulin, vanadate and ouabain on lipid synthesis in rat hepatocytes and the mechanism of these effects.
the effects of insulin, vanadate and ouabain on lipid synthesis in rat hepatocytes, and with the mechanism(s) of action of these compounds.
the effects of insulin, vanadate, and ouabain on lipid synthesis in isolated rat liver cells.

insulin and vanadium stimulate lipid synthesis in isolated rat liver cells through different mechanisms.
the stimulation of lipid synthesis by insulin and vanadium is not mediated by changes in the Ca2+ flux through plasma membrane.
insulin and vanadium stimulate lipogenesis in hepatocytes by mechanisms that are not mediated by changes in extracellular Ca2+ concentration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the stimulation of lipid synthesis in hepatocytes by insulin or vanadate is mediated by the activation of the phosphoinositide (PI) cycle and subsequent generation of inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate (IP3), but not of diacylglycerol (DG), whereas the inhibition of lipid synthesis by ouabain is due to a decrease in the cytoplasmic free calcium concentration.

vanadate is able to stimulate lipid synthesis, probably through a mechanism independent of Ca2+ flux through the cell surface, and this stimulation is not mimicked by the Ca2+-dependent insulin action.

the insulin effect on lipid synthesis is mediated by a protein kinase, which is activated by the phosphorylation of a protein, and this activation is not dependent on Ca2+ flux through the plasma membrane.

vanadate and insulin are able to increase lipid synthesis in hepatocytes and the effect of vanadate is much stronger than that of insulin.

insulin, vanadate, ouabain and their combinations have different effects on hepatic lipid synthesis, which may be useful to study the mechanism of lipid metabolism in hepatocytes and the role of Ca2+ in this process.
